Unfortunately , the amount of people who need to hedge do n't perfectly balance out . In come the speculators . Imagine you have a friend who loves playing with toys. You might notice that they always have a red toy car with them, and they like to play with blocks. Forensic psychologists do the same thing, but instead of toys, they look at people's actions and habits. 

For example, if a criminal always drives a red car, they might write that down in their profile. Or if a criminal likes to play video games, they might write that down too. This way, they can remember what the criminal might look like if they see them again. 

Forensic psychologists also use special tools to help them create these profiles. They might ask people a lot of questions to learn more about their habits and interests. Or they might use special tests to see how people behave in different situations. 

Once they have a profile, they can use it to help police find and catch criminals. For example, if they know a criminal always drives a red car, they can look for red cars in the area to see if they can find the criminal. Or if they know a criminal likes to play video games, they can look for places where video games are played.

The degree to which these profiles are accurate tends to increase with the number of data - points ( e.g. crime scenes ) that the profiler has to work with ( i.e. that are believed to be linked to the same offender ) . Profiling specific details ( e.g. a particular car model ) can not be done with any sort of accuracy unless the profiler has additional information ( e.g. physical evidence or eye - witness accounts ) which leads him / her to make such a conclusion . It is possible , however , that certain evidence may lead the profiler to suspect the criminal drives a certain type of vehicle . For example , evidence may suggest that the crime was politically motivated and the offender is an environmental protection activist . It may therefore be predicted that the offender drives an environmentally friendly electric / hybrid car . If , on the other hand , the criminal is suspected of being a hunter and weapons enthusiast , it may be predicted that he drives a utility truck of some sort which has lots of storage space . Criminal Profiling is still a hotly debated topic in Forensic Psychology because - although many profiles do turn out to be quite accurate - there are many criminals who are eventually caught and do n't end - up matching the predicted profile . The forensic utility of profiling is still questioned and it 's important for people to realize that these profiles are merely educated guesses and law enforcement should not eliminate or ignore suspects who do n't fit the suspected profile .
